blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Find the domain of the following: \(f(x) = \sin^{-1}(5x - 3)\).
blocks.explanation:
Domain ka matlab hai: \(x\) ki woh saari values jin par function defined ho (yani jawab nikal sake).
\(\sin^{-1}\) sirf \(-1\) se \(1\) tak ke input leta hai, kyunke kisi bhi angle ka sine is se bahar nahi jata.
Is liye poora input \(5x - 3\) bhi \([-1, 1]\) mein hona chahiye. Yeh double inequality solve karenge, bilkul Example 3 ki tarah.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \sin^{-1}(5x - 3)\).
Maloom karna: \(f\) ka domain.
Tareeqa: \(\sin^{-1} u\) ka domain \(-1 \le u \le 1\) hai. Yahan \(u = 5x - 3\) hai, to yahi shart \(5x - 3\) par lagayenge aur \(x\) ke liye solve karenge.

Shart likhein
\[-1 \le 5x - 3 \le 1\]
Kyun: \(\sin^{-1}\) ke andar jo bhi ho, woh \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan hona chahiye, warna aisa koi angle hi nahi jis ka sine woh number ho.

x ke liye solve karein
\[2 \le 5x \le 4\]
\[\frac{2}{5} \le x \le \frac{4}{5}\]
Kyun: Double inequality mein teenon hisson par ek jaisa kaam karte hain. Pehle teenon mein 3 jama kiya, phir teenon ko 5 se divide kiya. 5 positive hai, is liye inequality ke nishan nahi palte.
Dhyan dein: Sirf beech wale hisse par kaam kar ke kinaron ko bhool jana aam ghalti hai; teenon hisson par barabar amal karein.

Tasdeeq
\[x = \tfrac{2}{5}: \; 5x - 3 = -1\]
\[x = \tfrac{4}{5}: \; 5x - 3 = 1\]
Kyun: Kinare wali values par input bilkul \(-1\) aur \(1\) ban raha hai, jo allowed hain. Beech ki har value (maslan \(x = 0.6\), input \(0\)) bhi theek hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Find the domain of the following: \(g(x) = \cos^{-1}\sqrt{x - 3}\).
blocks.explanation:
Yahan do shartein hain. Pehli: square root ke andar wala hissa negative na ho, yani \(x - 3 \ge 0\).
Doosri: \(\cos^{-1}\) ka input \([-1, 1]\) mein ho.
Square root kabhi negative nahi hota, is liye doosri shart asal mein \(0 \le \sqrt{x - 3} \le 1\) ban jati hai. Phir square kar ke \(x\) nikal lenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(g(x) = \cos^{-1}\sqrt{x - 3}\).
Maloom karna: \(g\) ka domain.
Tareeqa: \(\sqrt{x - 3}\) real ho aur \([-1, 1]\) mein ho. Kyunke saare hisse non-negative (zero ya positive) honge, square karna mehfooz hai.

Square root ki shart
\[x - 3 \ge 0 \Rightarrow x \ge 3\]
Kyun: Negative number ka square root real nahi hota. Is liye \(x\) kam az kam 3 hona chahiye.

Inverse cosine ki shart
\[-1 \le \sqrt{x - 3} \le 1\]
\[0 \le \sqrt{x - 3} \le 1\]
Kyun: \(\cos^{-1}\) ka input \([-1, 1]\) mein hona chahiye. Lekin \(\sqrt{x - 3}\) hamesha \(0\) ya us se bara hota hai, is liye \(-1\) wala kinara khud ba khud poora hai; asal kinara \(0\) hai.

Square kar ke solve karein
\[0 \le x - 3 \le 1\]
\[3 \le x \le 4\]
Kyun: Jab saare hisse non-negative hon to square karne se inequality ka order nahi badalta. Phir teenon hisson mein 3 jama kiya.
Dhyan dein: Agar koi hissa negative ho to square karna khatarnak hai (maslan \(-2 < 1\) lekin \(4 > 1\)); yahan hum ne pehle \(0\) wala kinara bana kar yeh khatra khatam kar diya.

Tasdeeq
\[x = 4: \; \sqrt{1} = 1, \; \cos^{-1}1 = 0\]
\[x = 5: \; \sqrt{2} > 1 \text{ (not allowed)}\]
Kyun: \(x = 4\) par function defined hai, aur thora bahar \(x = 5\) par input 1 se bara ho jata hai. Is se pata chalta hai ke 4 hi aakhri value hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iii) Find the domain of the following: \(h(x) = \csc^{-1}(x^2 - 3)\).
blocks.explanation:
\(\csc^{-1}\) ka domain \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\) hai: input ya to \(-1\) ya us se chhota ho, ya \(1\) ya us se bara. Beech wale numbers (\(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan) mana hain, kyunke kisi angle ka cosecant wahan nahi aata.
Is liye do cases bante hain: \(x^2 - 3 \ge 1\) ya \(x^2 - 3 \le -1\).
Dono cases alag alag solve karenge aur phir union (dono ko jorna) lenge, kyunke shart mein 'ya' hai: koi bhi ek case poora ho jaye to kaafi hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(h(x) = \csc^{-1}(x^2 - 3)\).
Maloom karna: \(h\) ka domain.
Tareeqa: \(\csc^{-1} u\) ke liye \(u \le -1\) ya \(u \ge 1\) zaroori hai. \(u = x^2 - 3\) rakh kar har case solve karenge aur jawab jor denge.

Shart likhein
\[x^2 - 3 \ge 1 \quad \text{or} \quad x^2 - 3 \le -1\]
Kyun: Cosecant ki values \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke beech kabhi nahi aatin (graph mein beech wala khali band). Is liye \(\csc^{-1}\) ka input us band se bahar hona chahiye.

Case A
\[x^2 - 3 \ge 1 \Rightarrow x^2 \ge 4\]
\[(x - 2)(x + 2) \ge 0\]
\[x \le -2 \text{ or } x \ge 2\]
Kyun: 3 dono taraf jama kiya to \(x^2 \ge 4\) bana. Factor kiya: do cheezon ka product tab positive (ya zero) hota hai jab dono ka sign ek jaisa ho: dono negative (\(x \le -2\)) ya dono positive (\(x \ge 2\)).
Dhyan dein: \(x^2 \ge 4\) se sirf \(x \ge 2\) likh dena aadha jawab hai; negative side \(x \le -2\) bhi aati hai, kyunke \((-3)^2 = 9 \ge 4\).

Case B
\[x^2 - 3 \le -1 \Rightarrow x^2 \le 2\]
\[(x - \sqrt{2})(x + \sqrt{2}) \le 0\]
\[-\sqrt{2} \le x \le \sqrt{2}\]
Kyun: Is dafa product negative (ya zero) chahiye, jo tab hota hai jab factors ke sign ulat hon; yeh roots \(-\sqrt{2}\) aur \(\sqrt{2}\) ke beech hota hai.

Dono cases jorein
\[(-\infty, -2] \cup [-\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{2}] \cup [2, \infty)\]
Kyun: Shart mein 'ya' hai, is liye dono cases ki saari values domain mein hain; isay union kehte hain. Answer key ne sirf Case B likha hai, Case A chhoot gaya hai (neeche correction dekhiye).

Tasdeeq
\[x = 2: \; \csc^{-1}(1) = \tfrac{\pi}{2}\]
\[x = 0: \; \csc^{-1}(-3) \text{ exists}\]
\[x = 1.7: \; x^2 - 3 = -0.11 \text{ (not allowed)}\]
Kyun: Dono cases ki values (2 aur 0) par function chal raha hai, lekin \(1.7\) jaisi value, jo \(\sqrt{2} \approx 1.41\) aur 2 ke beech hai, input ko mana band mein le jati hai. Figure mein bhi parabola ka wohi hissa band ke andar hai.

answer_figure.alt: Parabola y = x squared minus 3 with the band between y = minus 1 and y = 1 shaded. The curve is allowed where it is outside the band: for x at most minus 2, between minus root 2 and root 2, and for x at least 2. These three pieces are marked in green on the x-axis.
answer_figure.caption: h ka domain: parabola y = x² − 3 ko band −1 < y < 1 se bahar rehna hai (original drawing).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key mein sirf \(-\sqrt{2} \le x \le \sqrt{2}\) likha hai. Yeh adhoora jawab hai: yeh sirf Case B hai. Case A (\(x^2 - 3 \ge 1\), yani \(|x| \ge 2\)) bhool gaye hain, halanke maslan \(h(2) = \csc^{-1}(1) = \frac{\pi}{2}\) bilkul defined hai. Sahi domain \((-\infty, -2] \cup [-\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{2}] \cup [2, \infty)\) hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iv) Find the domain of the following: \(k(x) = \sin^{-1}(\ln x)\).
blocks.explanation:
Yahan bhi do shartein hain. Pehli: \(\ln x\) sirf positive \(x\) ke liye defined hai, yani \(x > 0\).
Doosri: \(\sin^{-1}\) ka input \([-1, 1]\) mein ho, yani \(-1 \le \ln x \le 1\).
Logarithm ko hatane ke liye us ka ulta function, exponential \(e^{(\,)}\), teenon hisson par lagayenge, bilkul Example 3(iii) ki tarah.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(k(x) = \sin^{-1}(\ln x)\).
Maloom karna: \(k\) ka domain.
Tareeqa: \(x > 0\) aur \(-1 \le \ln x \le 1\) dono chahiye. Teenon hisson ko \(e\) ki power bana denge.

Shart likhein
\[-1 \le \ln x \le 1\]
Kyun: \(\sin^{-1}\) ke andar jo bhi ho, woh \([-1, 1]\) mein hona chahiye; yahan andar \(\ln x\) hai.

Logarithm hatayein
\[e^{-1} \le e^{\ln x} \le e^{1}\]
\[\frac{1}{e} \le x \le e\]
Kyun: \(e^{t}\) increasing function hai (jitna bara \(t\), utna bara \(e^{t}\)), is liye teenon hisson par lagane se nishan wohi rehte hain. Aur \(e^{\ln x} = x\), kyunke dono ek doosre ke ulte functions hain.
Dhyan dein: \(e^{-1}\) ka matlab \(\frac{1}{e} \approx 0.37\) hai, \(-e\) nahi.

Log wali shart
\[\frac{1}{e} > 0\]
Kyun: Jo \(x\) mile woh sab \(\frac{1}{e}\) se bare hain, yani positive hain. Is liye \(x > 0\) wali shart pehle hi poori ho chuki hai; kuch kaatna nahi para.

Tasdeeq
\[x = e: \; \sin^{-1}(\ln e) = \sin^{-1}1 = \tfrac{\pi}{2}\]
Kyun: \(\ln e = 1\), aur \(\sin^{-1} 1 = \frac{\pi}{2}\) defined hai. Isi tarah \(x = \frac{1}{e}\) par \(\ln x = -1\) aata hai, woh bhi allowed hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (v) Find the domain of the following: \(p(x) = \tan^{-1}\sqrt{4 - x^2}\).
blocks.explanation:
\(\tan^{-1}\) har real number ko input ke tor par qubool karta hai (us ka domain \((-\infty, \infty)\) hai), is liye us ki taraf se koi pabandi nahi.
Pabandi sirf square root ki hai: andar wala hissa \(4 - x^2\) negative nahi hona chahiye.
Yani asal sawal sirf ek quadratic inequality ka hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(p(x) = \tan^{-1}\sqrt{4 - x^2}\).
Maloom karna: \(p\) ka domain.
Tareeqa: \(\tan^{-1}\) ka domain poori real line hai, is liye sirf square root ki shart \(4 - x^2 \ge 0\) solve karni hai.

Square root ki shart
\[4 - x^2 \ge 0 \Rightarrow x^2 \le 4\]
Kyun: Negative number ka square root real nahi hota. \(x^2\) ko doosri taraf le gaye to \(x^2 \le 4\) bana.

Solve karein
\[(x - 2)(x + 2) \le 0\]
\[-2 \le x \le 2\]
Kyun: Product zero ya negative tab hota hai jab factors ke sign ulat hon, aur aisa roots \(-2\) aur \(2\) ke beech hota hai.
Dhyan dein: \(x^2 \le 4\) se \(x \le 2\) likh dena ghalat hai, kyunke \(x = -5\) bhi \(x \le 2\) hai magar \((-5)^2 = 25 > 4\).

Tasdeeq
\[x = 2: \; \tan^{-1}\sqrt{0} = 0\]
\[x = 3: \; \sqrt{-5} \text{ is not real}\]
Kyun: Kinare par function defined hai, aur thora bahar jate hi square root ke andar negative aa jata hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (vi) Find the domain of the following: \(q(x) = \sec^{-1}(x + 2)\).
blocks.explanation:
\(\sec^{-1}\) ka input \(-1\) ya us se chhota, ya \(1\) ya us se bara hona chahiye; beech wale numbers mana hain.
Is liye \(x + 2 \le -1\) ya \(x + 2 \ge 1\). Dono simple linear inequalities hain.
Dono ko solve kar ke union lenge, kyunke koi bhi ek case kaafi hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(q(x) = \sec^{-1}(x + 2)\).
Maloom karna: \(q\) ka domain.
Tareeqa: \(\sec^{-1} u\) ka domain \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\) hai. \(u = x + 2\) rakh kar do cases banayenge.

Case A
\[x + 2 \le -1 \Rightarrow x \le -3\]
Kyun: Dono taraf se 2 minus kiya; minus karne se inequality ka nishan nahi badalta.

Case B
\[x + 2 \ge 1 \Rightarrow x \ge -1\]
Kyun: Phir dono taraf se 2 minus kiya.

Cases jorein
\[(-\infty, -3] \cup [-1, \infty)\]
Kyun: Shart mein 'ya' hai, is liye dono hisson ka union domain hai.
Dhyan dein: Yahan intersection (\(\cap\)) lena ghalat hoga; dono cases ek saath sach ho hi nahi sakte, intersection khali aata.

Tasdeeq
\[x = -2: \; x + 2 = 0 \text{ (not allowed)}\]
Kyun: \(-3\) aur \(-1\) ke beech ki koi value lein, input \((-1, 1)\) mein aa jata hai, jahan \(\sec^{-1}\) defined nahi. Is liye yahi hissa domain se bahar hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (vii) Find the domain of the following: \(u(x) = \sec^{-1}\left(\frac{3x - 1}{2}\right)\).
blocks.explanation:
Pichle part ki tarah \(\sec^{-1}\) ka input \(\le -1\) ya \(\ge 1\) hona chahiye.
Yahan input ek fraction \(\frac{3x - 1}{2}\) hai. Dono cases mein pehle 2 se multiply kar ke fraction khatam karenge, phir \(x\) nikalenge.
Aakhir mein dono hisson ka union lenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(u(x) = \sec^{-1}\left(\frac{3x - 1}{2}\right)\).
Maloom karna: \(u\) ka domain.
Tareeqa: \(\sec^{-1}\) ka domain \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\) hai. Har case ko 2 (positive number) se multiply kar ke solve karenge.

Case A
\[\frac{3x - 1}{2} \le -1\]
\[3x - 1 \le -2 \Rightarrow 3x \le -1\]
\[x \le -\frac{1}{3}\]
Kyun: 2 se multiply kiya (positive hai, nishan wohi), phir 1 jama kiya, phir 3 se divide kiya. Har qadam positive number ke saath tha, is liye \(\le\) wohi raha.

Case B
\[\frac{3x - 1}{2} \ge 1\]
\[3x - 1 \ge 2 \Rightarrow 3x \ge 3\]
\[x \ge 1\]
Kyun: Bilkul wohi qadam: 2 se multiply, 1 jama, 3 se divide.

Cases jorein
\[\left(-\infty, -\frac{1}{3}\right] \cup [1, \infty)\]
Kyun: Shart mein 'ya' hai, is liye union.
Dhyan dein: Agar kabhi negative number se multiply ya divide karna pare to inequality ka nishan ulta karna parta hai; yahan aisa koi qadam nahi aaya.

Tasdeeq
\[x = 1: \; \tfrac{3 - 1}{2} = 1, \; \sec^{-1}1 = 0\]
\[x = 0: \; -\tfrac{1}{2} \text{ (not allowed)}\]
Kyun: Kinare \(x = 1\) par input bilkul 1 hai jo allowed hai; beech ki value \(x = 0\) par input \(-\frac{1}{2}\) mana band mein hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (viii) Find the domain of the following: \(v(x) = \sin^{-1}(\ln x) + \csc^{-1}(e^{x})\).
blocks.explanation:
Do terms ka jama tabhi defined hota hai jab dono terms alag alag defined hon. Agar ek bhi term ka jawab na nikle to jama bhi nahi nikal sakta.
Is liye har term ka domain alag nikalenge, phir dono ka intersection (mushtarka hissa, \(\cap\)) lenge.
Yaad rakhiye: ek hi inverse function ke do cases (jaise \(\le -1\) ya \(\ge 1\)) ho to union, lekin do alag terms ka jama ho to intersection.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(v(x) = \sin^{-1}(\ln x) + \csc^{-1}(e^{x})\).
Maloom karna: \(v\) ka domain.
Tareeqa: Jama ka domain = dono terms ke domains ka intersection. Pehla term part (iv) jaisa hai, doosre term ke liye \(\csc^{-1}\) ki shart lagayenge.

Pehla term
\[-1 \le \ln x \le 1 \Rightarrow \frac{1}{e} \le x \le e\]
Kyun: Yeh bilkul part (iv) hai: teenon hisson par increasing function \(e^{t}\) lagaya, nishan wohi rahe, aur \(e^{\ln x} = x\).

Doosra term
\[e^{x} \le -1 \quad \text{or} \quad e^{x} \ge 1\]
\[e^{x} \ge 1 = e^{0} \Rightarrow x \ge 0\]
Kyun: \(\csc^{-1}\) ka input \(\le -1\) ya \(\ge 1\) hona chahiye. Lekin \(e^{x}\) hamesha positive hota hai, is liye \(e^{x} \le -1\) mumkin hi nahi. Bacha \(e^{x} \ge 1 = e^{0}\); \(e^{x}\) increasing hai, to \(x \ge 0\).
Dhyan dein: \(e^{x} \ge 1\) se \(x \ge 1\) likh dena aam ghalti hai; \(e^{0} = 1\) hai, is liye sahi shart \(x \ge 0\) hai.

Intersection
\[\left[\frac{1}{e}, e\right] \cap [0, \infty)\]
\[= \left[\frac{1}{e}, e\right]\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{e} \approx 0.37\), jo 0 se bara hai. Yani pehla interval poora ka poora \([0, \infty)\) ke andar hai; mushtarka hissa wohi pehla interval hai. Figure mein teesri line yahi dikhati hai.

Tasdeeq
\[x = \tfrac{1}{e}: \; \ln x = -1, \; e^{x} \approx 1.44 \ge 1\]
Kyun: Baayen kinare par dono terms defined hain, is liye \(\frac{1}{e}\) domain mein shamil hai. Is liye answer key ka jawab \(\left[\frac{1}{e}, e\right]\) bilkul sahi hai.

answer_figure.alt: Three number lines. The first marks the closed interval from 1 over e (about 0.37) to e (about 2.72) needed by inverse sine of ln x. The second marks x greater than or equal to 0 needed by inverse cosecant of e to the x. The third shows their common part, the interval from 1 over e to e.
answer_figure.caption: v ka domain: dono alag domains ka mushtarka hissa (intersection) (original drawing).
